deep.reconstruction:
This page has no derivation. It is a topical outline in pencil, probably notes taken at, or prepared for, a course in experimental physics or hydraulics. It continues the previous page, which dealt with wave motion on a stretched string (speed sqrt(g*l), with the tension expressed as a weight-column of height l), Torricelli's outflow law v^2 = 2 g h, U-tube motion, and Segner's wheel. The items, in modern terms:

(a) Outflow through horizontal walls, upward jets. An ideal vertical jet rises to the pressure head h = v^2/(2g), which is Torricelli read backwards. The listed demonstration devices are Hero's ball (Heronsball), the fire pump (Feuerspritze) and Hero's fountain (Heronsbrunnen).

(b) Resistance (absolute vs. practical) in fluid flow, i.e. the gap between ideal outflow and real discharge coefficients. Reichenbach's current-velocity meter, a hydrometric instrument for measuring stream speed.

(c) Restoration of the original water level, i.e. return to equilibrium after a disturbance.

(d) Wave motion, treated experimentally:
  1/ the speed of propagation of the waves;
  2/ counting the individual waves; the oscillation speed of standing waves is 'theoretically found';
  3/ standing waves. In modern terms these are a superposition of counter-propagating waves: sin(kx-wt) + sin(kx+wt) = 2 sin(kx) cos(wt).

(e) The elliptic shape (of particle paths or wave form) at a boundary point. Whether wave propagation depends on direction. Deflection at an interface (reflection/refraction).

(f) D'Alembert's principle, listed as the general dynamical foundation.

None of these items is worked out on the page. They are headings only. The next page switches to Riemann's own lecture material on PDEs: the heat equation solved by the Gaussian kernel and its Fourier form, and the Laplace equation with the Dirichlet-principle argument.
